review: 304.4: skip reason was wrong (a manifested instant exiled and returned, e.g. by Cloudshift, would enter the battlefield face up); added scenario 304.4-1 and removed the skip.
304.5-1: setup notes said Silence had already resolved while Silence was still in B's hand and cast in the decisions; notes corrected.

scenarios.title: An instant can be cast whenever its controller has priority; a sorcery cannot

setup.notes: B is the active player; B has passed priority with an empty stack and A has priority.

decisions: The candidate action is A casting Lightning Bolt from hand, paying {R} with a Mountain.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Casting Lightning Bolt is legal: can_play is true, though it is B's turn and a combat step.

variants.label: with-stack
variants.delta: B has first cast Shock targeting A, tapping B's Mountain, and A has priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Casting Lightning Bolt is legal: can_play is true while Shock is on the stack.

variants.label: sorcery
variants.delta: The candidate is A casting Lava Axe (a sorcery) instead of Lightning Bolt, paying {4}{R} with the five Mountains.
variants.expected: Casting Lava Axe is not legal: can_play is false, because it is not a main phase of A's turn.

scenarios.title: A resolving instant follows its text and then goes to its owner's graveyard
decisions: A casts Shock targeting B, tapping the Mountain.
A passes priority; B passes priority; Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Shock deals 2 damage to B, whose life total is 18, and then moves from the stack to A's graveyard.

variants.label: countered
variants.delta: After A passes priority B casts Counterspell targeting Shock, tapping both Islands, then both players pass.
variants.expected: Shock is countered: its text is not followed, B's life total stays 20, and Shock moves from the stack to A's graveyard; Counterspell goes to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: A manifested instant that is exiled and returned to the battlefield stays in exile

setup.notes: The face-down card was manifested by A on an earlier turn (a 2/2 face-down creature, not turned face up).

decisions: A casts Cloudshift targeting the face-down creature, tapping the Plains.
A passes priority; B passes priority; Cloudshift resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The face-down creature is exiled and turns face up as Lightning Bolt; Lightning Bolt cannot enter the battlefield and stays in A's exile; Cloudshift goes to A's graveyard.

variants.label: creature-card
variants.delta: The manifested card is Grizzly Bears instead of Lightning Bolt.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is exiled and returns to the battlefield face up under A's control as a 2/2; Cloudshift goes to A's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: GameAction.changeZone refuses instants and sorceries moving to the battlefield. The face-down state must be a manifest, not a morph.

scenarios.title: An action usable 'only as an instant' needs priority, even when the player cannot cast spells

setup.notes: It is B's upkeep and B has priority with an empty stack; Silence is still in B's hand and is cast in the decisions.

decisions: B casts Silence, tapping the Plains; both players pass; Silence resolves.
B passes priority and A receives priority.
The candidate action is A activating Lion's Eye Diamond ('Sacrifice, discard your hand: add three mana of any one color. Activate only as an instant').

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The activation is legal: can_play is true, because A has priority, although A cannot cast spells.

variants.label: cast-instant
variants.delta: The candidate is A casting the instant Shock with the Mountain instead.
variants.expected: Casting Shock is not legal: can_play is false, because Silence stops A from casting spells.

scenarios.forge_notes: Lion's Eye Diamond is a mana ability, so the activation does not use the stack; its playability verdict is the legality of activating it.
